questions.label: 2(a)
questions.stem:
An ice sculpture melts in such a way that it can be modeled as a cone that maintains a conical shape as it decreases in size. The radius of the base of the cone is given by a twice-differentiable function $r$, where $r(t)$ is measured in centimeters and $t$ is measured in days. The table gives selected values of $r'(t)$, the rate of change of the radius, over the time interval $0\leqslant t\leqslant12$. $$\begin{array}{|c|c|c|c|c|c|}\hline t\text{ (days)} & 0 & 3 & 7 & 10 & 12\\ \hline r'(t)\text{ (centimeters per day)} & -6.1 & -5.0 & -4.4 & -3.8 & -3.5\\ \hline\end{array}$$

Approximate $r''(8.5)$ using the average rate of change of $r'$ over the interval $7\leqslant t\leqslant10$. Show the computations that lead to your answer, and indicate units of measure.

questions.label: 2(b)
questions.stem:

questions.label: 7(a)
questions.stem:
Select values of the twice differentiable function $n$ are given in the table. The function $p$ is the piecewise function made up of the quarter circle, $y=\sqrt{4-x^2}$ and two line segments, all as shown in the graph. A third function, $r$, is defined analytically as a piecewise function.
$$\begin{array}{|l|c|c|}\hline x & n(x) & n\prime(x) \\ \hline -2 & -2 & 2 \\ \hline -1 & 1 & 1 \\ \hline \tfrac12 & 2 & 1 \\ \hline 1 & \tfrac12 & -2 \\ \hline 3 & -1 & 2 \\ \hline\end{array}$$
$$r(x)=\begin{cases}2x+4&x<-1\\-x^3+1&-1\le x\le1\\x^2+\sin x&x>1.\end{cases}$$
[Source discrepancy: the printed quarter-circle formula is positive, but the pictured quarter circle lies below the $x$-axis. The graph shows $p(x)=-\sqrt{4-x^2}$ for $-2\le x\le0$. The solutions below use the pictured graph; the requested evaluations do not use that quarter-circle branch.]

Use continuity to show that $r(x)$ is not differentiable at $x=1$.

figures.alt: Graph of p: closed (-2,0), lower quarter circle to (0,-2), horizontal segment to (2,-2), line segment to closed (4,4).

questions.label: 18(a)
questions.stem:
Let $f(x)=\begin{cases}\frac{2x^2+5x-3}{x^2+4x+3}&x<-3\\kx+\frac12&-3\le x\le0\\\frac{2^x}{3^x-1}&x>0.\end{cases}$ Let $f$ be the function defined above, where $k$ is a constant.

For what value of $k$, if any, is $f$ continuous at $x=-3$? Justify your answer.

questions.label: 18(b)
questions.stem:
Let $f(x)=\begin{cases}\frac{2x^2+5x-3}{x^2+4x+3}&x<-3\\kx+\frac12&-3\le x\le0\\\frac{2^x}{3^x-1}&x>0.\end{cases}$ Let $f$ be the function defined above, where $k$ is a constant.

What type of discontinuity does $f$ have at $x=0$? Give a reason for your answer.
